title: Introduce token-burst fingerprinting and adaptive alert thresholds for long-tail surge detection
author: Asha Patel
release_notes: Adds token-burst detection metric and dashboard; introduces adaptive alert thresholds for long-tail cost/latency surges. Backwards-compatible. Requires alert rule update in prod after rollout.
performance_impact: minor CPU on telemetry ingest (0.5%-1%); negligible on serving path; batched evaluation removed from fast path by default
description: Motivation: we continue to see sporadic long-tail bursts where a small subset of invocations generate sudden token spikes that materially increase per-tenant unit cost and SLO burn. Existing static alert thresholds cause either noisy paging or missed incidents during workload drift. This PR introduces a lightweight token-burst fingerprint and an adaptive alert threshold pipeline that reduces false positives while still surfacing high-impact bursts. Changes: 1) token_burst_detector: new streaming detector that computes a compact fingerprint for bursty invocations using an epochal sliding histogram and decaying reservoir aggregation; the fingerprint is a short static key useful for grouping repeated burst patterns. 2) adaptive_thresholds: a controller that computes per-route and per-tenant z-score thresholds on rolling windows (configurable: 1h/6h/24h) and exposes candidate alert thresholds to the alerting service via a feature-flagged endpoint. 3) dashboards: new Grafana dashboard (Token Burst Explorer) with burst fingerprint heatmap, per-route epochal histograms, and an automated remediation suggestion panel. 4) alerts: a new alert rule bundle that can operate in 'suggest' or 'enforce' mode; initially rolled out in suggest mode to gather telemetry. 5) small SDK enrichment: attach burst_fingerprint to traces/logs as attribute "burst.fingerprint" and to metric labels for correlation. Backwards compatibility: detectors are opt-in per-tenant via the telemetry feature flag. Rollout plan: canary 5% of traffic in staging -> suggest-mode in prod for 24h -> adapt thresholds based on observed false positive reduction -> enforce mode for tenants that opt-in. Notes on cost and performance: detector runs as a sidecar on telemetry ingest nodes; it processes derived token counts and does not alter the serving runtime or KV cache hot path. Tests: unit tests for histogram synthesis and fingerprint collision properties; end-to-end smoke that validates dashboard panels; a perf microbenchmark validates <1% CPU overhead on typical ingest nodes. See commits and files changed for details.

summary_of_changes: Implements token-burst detection and adaptive alert thresholds; wires fingerprint into traces and metrics; adds dashboard and alert bundle; includes tests and benchmarks.
testing_notes: Unit tests cover histogram synthesis, collision rate for fingerprinting (<1/1e6 on synthetic workloads), and threshold controller convergence. Benchmarks show <1% CPU on telemetry ingest in a 10k req/s synthetic replay. Recommend staging canary for 48h before full rollout.
operational_notes: Feature flag: telemetry.token_burst.enabled (default: false). Alert rule supports 'mode: suggest|enforce'. When switching to enforce, update alert routing to include cost-on-call for first 7 days. Ops runbook path: ops/runbooks/observability.md#token-burst-fingerprint
backwards_compatibility: The detector is opt-in; metric labels have been kept low-cardinality (tenant_hash) and a migration note is included. No serving API changes.
follow_up_tasks: ENG-10488: add anomaly feedback loop to auto-tune sensitivity; ENG-10512: integrate with billing pipeline to flag high-cost bursts for account review; add RBAC guard for threshold override UI.
manual_steps_for_release: 1) Enable telemetry.token_burst.enabled=true for staging canary tenants. 2) Deploy alert bundle in suggest mode. 3) Monitor Token Burst Explorer dashboard for 24-48h. 4) Flip specific tenant alerts to enforce via ops runbook.
changelog_entry: Added token-burst fingerprint detector and adaptive alert thresholds for long-tail surge detection (observability).
access_notes: Telemetry team and SREs only for initial rollout; dashboard viewable by internal teams.
